title: “Monks, if wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ — being asked thus,…
content: “Monks, if wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ — being asked thus, monks, you should answer them: ‘For the purpose of the destruction of greed, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ Then, monks, if they ask: ‘Is there, friends, a path, a way for the destruction of greed?’ — being asked thus, you should answer: ‘There is a path, a way for the destruction of greed.’ And what, monks, is that path, that way? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view … right concentration. This, monks, is the path, the way for the destruction of greed. Being asked thus, monks, you should answer them in that way.”

title: “Those who day and night Devote themselves to the teaching Of the Perfectly Enlightened One — They calm the fire of greed By always perceiving…
content:
“Those who day and night
Devote themselves to the teaching
Of the Perfectly Enlightened One —
They calm the fire of greed
By always perceiving the foul.

With the mind of loving-kindness, the supreme,
They calm the fire of hatred.
With the fire of delusion,
By wisdom they extinguish it —
Wisdom that leads to penetration.

Ardent, mindful,
Day and night they calm
These fires without remainder —
They make them cease without remainder.

Those noble ones who have seen,
The wise with knowledge,
Having rightly known the destruction of birth,
Do not go to renewed existence.”

title: “‘Empty is the world, empty is the world,’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is it said that the world is empty?”…
content: “‘Empty is the world, empty is the world,’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is it said that the world is empty?” - “Ānanda, because the world is empty of self and anything belonging to self, therefore it is said that the world is empty. And what, Ānanda, is empty of self and anything belonging to self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of self and anything belonging to self. Forms are empty of self and anything belonging to self. Eye-consciousness … Eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … that feeling is empty of self and anything belonging to self. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind … Phenomena … Mind-consciousness … Mind-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact … that feeling is empty of self and anything belonging to self. And because it is empty of self and anything belonging to self, Ānanda, it is said that the world is empty.”

title: “O good friends, here someone associates with sensual pleasures, associates with unwholesome states. After some time, that person hears the noble Dhamma, gives wise attention,…
content: “O good friends, here someone associates with sensual pleasures, associates with unwholesome states. After some time, that person hears the noble Dhamma, gives wise attention, and attains the true Dhamma and the Dhamma in accordance. And having heard the noble Dhamma, given wise attention, and attained the true Dhamma and the Dhamma in accordance, that person lives without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states. By living without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states, ease arises, and more than ease, gladness arises. O good friends, just as from comfort joy is born, so too, O good friends, by living without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states, ease arises, and more than ease, gladness arises. O good friends, that is the first short path leading to ease, realized by the Blessed One, the Wise One, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

title: “Therefore, monks, abandon the unwholesome and strive for the wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Monks,…
content: “Therefore, monks, abandon the unwholesome and strive for the wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Monks, just as near a village or small town there is a large sala-tree forest overgrown with trumpet-flower creepers. Then a man comes who desires the welfare of that forest, its benefit, its security from bondage. He cuts down the crooked, weak branches, throws them out, and cleans the forest inside. He properly cares for the straight, well-grown sala saplings. Monks, after some time, that forest becomes grown, prosperous, and increased. So too, monks, abandon the unwholesome and strive for the wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

title: “Monks, just as in a dense forest there is a large deep lake, and a great herd of deer lives near one side. Then a…
content: “Monks, just as in a dense forest there is a large deep lake, and a great herd of deer lives near one side. Then a man comes who does not desire their welfare, does not desire their benefit, does not desire their security from bondage. He closes off the safe, secure path leading to happiness and opens a dangerous path, sets a male decoy and a female decoy. Monks, then that great herd of deer will later fall into bondage and decline. Monks, then a man comes who desires their welfare, desires their benefit, desires their security from bondage. He opens the safe, secure path, closes the dangerous path, removes the male decoy, and destroys the female decoy. Monks, then that great herd of deer will later increase, prosper, and become abundant.”

title: “If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome,…
content: “If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome, monks, is just the five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. Indeed, the entire heap of the unwholesome is just the five hindrances.”

title: “Venerable Gotama, I have a perplexity and doubt: ‘How should one understand the Dhamma of the ascetic Gotama?’” - “Vaccha, your perplexity is enough, your…
content: “Venerable Gotama, I have a perplexity and doubt: ‘How should one understand the Dhamma of the ascetic Gotama?’” - “Vaccha, your perplexity is enough, your doubt is enough. It is on this point that perplexity and doubt have arisen. I declare the rebirth of one who has clinging, Vaccha, not of one who has no clinging. Just as, Vaccha, a fire burns when there is fuel, not when there is no fuel. So too, Vaccha, I declare rebirth for one who has clinging, not for one who has no clinging.” - “Venerable Gotama, when the wind blows a fire far away, what does Venerable Gotama declare as the fuel for that fire?” - “Vaccha, when the wind blows a fire far away, I say that the wind is its fuel. At that time, Vaccha, the wind is the fuel (upādāna).” - “Venerable Gotama, when a being gives up this body and is reborn in another body, what does Venerable Gotama declare as the fuel for that being?” - “Vaccha, when a being gives up this body and is reborn in another body, I declare that at that time craving (taṇhā) is the fuel (upādāna).”

title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? Because of what is there no liberation? - Craving gives birth…
content:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
Because of what is there no liberation?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Because of suffering, there is no liberation.

title: - Who ages, who does not age? What is called the wrong path? What is an obstacle to the Dhamma? What destroys day and night?…
content:
- Who ages, who does not age?
What is called the wrong path?
What is an obstacle to the Dhamma?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
How many openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell?
I have come to ask the Blessed One —
Please tell me the answers!
- Form in beings ages,
The name-nature does not age,
Greed is called the wrong path,
Craving is an obstacle to the Dhamma.
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life —
Ensnared in this defilement
Are all beings.
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.
There are six openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell:
Laziness and heedlessness,
Lethargy and lack of self-control,
Drowsiness and sloth —
These six openings should be
Completely abandoned.
